item.title: RESIGNATION IS NOT FUCKING ACCOUNTABILITY.
item.description:
A one-year-old child is dead. Kohen Wiley was killed when Senatobia police officer Hunter Foster fired three shots during a confrontation in a Walmart parking lot.
Now, following the release of body-camera footage, Foster has resigned. And that's supposed to be where the story ends? A badge isn't a shield from accountability. A resignation isn't a verdict. And handing in your uniform doesn't answer the questions a grieving family deserves to have answered. If the shooting was justified, let the evidence withstand independent scrutiny. If laws were broken, prosecute accordingly. Because a child doesn't get to come home simply because an officer no longer reports for duty. Kohen Wiley deserved a future. His family deserves answers. #JusticeForKohenWiley #PoliceAccountability #JusticeForKohen #Transparency #Accountability #StreetArt #StencilArt #PoliticalStreetArt #ArtAsProtest #ProtestArt #Artivism #VisualSatire #SocialCommentary #ArtWithAMessage

item.title: GovBrief Today #631
item.description: Donald Trump ordered the Justice Department to sue Alaska so it can’t certify its Senate race if Republican Dan Sullivan loses. “I’m the one that said, ‘do it,’” he told reporters Friday. The suit claims Alaskans can’t tell their senator apart from a retired schoolteacher with the same name, though the ballot labels one of them the incumbent and the state’s Supreme Court already ruled both could run. No president before him has asked a court to throw out an election’s results before there were any. This week, Attorney General Todd Blanche wouldn’t rule out the department blocking a state’s certification in what he called a “doomsday scenario.” The last time a certification stood in Trump’s way, a mob broke into the Capitol and sent senators and representatives fleeing. This time the Justice Department filed the paperwork. I’ve emailed 9,656 stories over 631 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can’t show them all to you.
